title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices in Financial Literacy among Business Administration Students in Urban College in the Philippines
tldr: Business administration students show positive attitudes toward financial literacy but knowledge and practices vary significantly by age, sex, income, and year level.
problem_and_motivation: Financial literacy among business students is increasingly important due to complex financial products and economic uncertainty, but curriculum gaps in financial education persist.
approach: Survey-based quantitative approach assessing financial literacy knowledge, attitudes, and practices.
Respondents: Business Administration students in urban Philippine college.
Analyzes demographic factors: age, sex, monthly income, and year level.
Statistical tests for significant differences and relationships.
findings: Students generally have a positive attitude toward financial literacy.
Knowledge varies significantly by age, sex, and year level.
Attitude varies significantly by age, monthly income, and year level.
Practice varies significantly by age, sex, monthly income, and year level.
Significant relationship between knowledge, attitude, and practices (R=0.697, p=0.000).
key_figures_tables: Table 5: Practices by demographic profile → All demographic factors significant.
Table 6: Relationship among knowledge, attitude, practices → R=0.697, p=0.000, significant.
